acceptanceCriteria: Without a subject, lexical rows are ordered by match strength, not a flat score.
A selected source file's paired test is admitted ahead of unrelated lexical tests within the limit.
The frozen retrieval evaluations do not regress, and the change is validated on a held-out repository whose cases were frozen before the fix ran against it.
body: Observed in V1-0019 run-001 on go-chi/chi with the 1.0.0-rc.1 candidate b967f6bb (binary sha256 baac3385...): UC-TASK-ORIENTATION FAILED with 3 treatment-only critical misses. Case b1c9ab47 (task `record response status when flushing`): `corvint context --task ... --limit 20` returned middleware/wrap_writer.go but not middleware/wrap_writer_test.go, while 10 unrelated *_test.go files filled the packet; plain git grep included it. Case 50ef4e4c (`Replace "interface{}" with "any"`) missed middleware/middleware_test.go and middleware/recoverer_test.go. Diagnosis on b1c9ab47^: the task names no file, so the subject-anchored slots (pair, reverse-import, reference, cochange, sibling) report subject-absent; one `test` row (score 700) and 19 `lexical` rows all at score 300 fill the packet, so lexical order among ties is not by match strength and the pair slot never runs for a lexical hit (internal/contextindex/taskcontext.go contextPairCap, contextTestCap). The preregistration forbids tuning the scored candidate, so the fix lands in a later candidate and is validated on a new held-out repository (owner answer 2026-09-27: spf13/cobra).
title: Task context without a subject scores every lexical row equally and never adds a selected file's paired test
